witness.title: Protecting Witnesses
witness.text: Asking a colleague to be a witness can be scary. Remember, you don't have to demand that they "choose a side".

list: Log: "Witness A (team member) confirmed the issue."
Ask HR for an anonymized summary.
Ask neutrally: "Would it be ok to tell about your observations if asked?"
Give a way out: "I understand well if you don't want to."
Don't pressure: Fear of retaliation is real. Respect it.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Unsure about something? Here are answers to common questions.
faq.a1: Turvasiipi is a free digital tool for documenting, identifying, and addressing workplace bullying and inappropriate treatment. We provide information, tools, and peer support to everyone who encounters inappropriate behavior.
faq.q2: Who sees the things I write?
faq.a2: No one but you. All information is stored only on your own device (phone or computer). We don't have a server that collects your data, nor do we see your logbooks or reports.
faq.q3: Can my employer see that I use this?
faq.a3: No. The app doesn't require logging in with work email, nor does it leave traces on the company's network (except browser history). We recommend using the app on your own device or in Private Browsing (Incognito) mode.
faq.a4: You record events in the "Timeline" section. The information is saved in your device's memory. When you need evidence, you can create an automatic PDF summary of all your entries in the "Report" section, for example for occupational health or safety.
faq.q5: Is the story I share in the Stories section visible to others?
faq.a5: Yes, but only if you choose to publish it. Publishing is fully anonymous (or with a pseudonym of your choice). We don't store IP addresses, so stories cannot be traced back to you.
faq.q6: I am in immediate danger. What should I do?
faq.a6: If you experience violence or an acute threat, call the emergency number 112 immediately. Turvasiipi is a documentation tool, not a crisis service. In mental distress, call the Crisis Hotline: 010 195 202.
faq.q7: How does Turvasiipi help me recover?
faq.a7: Beyond passive documentation, the app provides active tools: simulators and coaching modules. They allow you to practice difficult situations safely, strengthen your resilience, and learn to set boundaries tactically.
faq.a9_text: Bullying literacy is the ability to recognize, understand, and confront bullying in the work community – in time and together. It:
faq.a9_list_1: Identifies latent and subtle forms of bullying.
faq.a9_list_2: Understands the dynamics and effects of the phenomenon.
faq.a10: Turvasiipi is designed for everyone who wants to understand workplace power dynamics and recognize latent psychological violence.

BACKGROUND
I have been working at [Company] in [Role] since [Start Date]. Over the past [Period], I have experienced systematic inappropriate treatment that affects my occupational safety and health.

EVENTS
[AI combination of events]

IMPACT
Curated treatment described above has caused me significant burden, manifested as [AI symptoms: e.g. sleep problems and decreased work vigor].

career-interview-prep.title: Answering in job interviews
career-interview-prep.description: How to explain changing jobs without being labeled a "difficult employee".
career-interview-prep.subject: Job interview response template (oral)
career-interview-prep.content:
GENERAL RULE: Do not badmouth your previous employer. Focus on the future.

OPTION A (Neutral):
"In my previous employment, I identified that the organizational culture and management style no longer matched my values or enabled my development. Therefore, I decided to seek an environment where open communication and cooperation are valued, as they are here."

OPTION B (Slightly more open):
"In my previous job, a challenging management situation was encountered. I did my best to resolve the situation, but ultimately concluded that it is best to move on and focus energy on a new challenge."

OPTION C (Honest):
"I experienced inappropriate treatment at my previous workplace, which despite efforts, could not be resolved. I documented the situation carefully and handled my departure professionally. This experience has taught me a lot about a healthy work culture and how important mutual respect is."

comm-thanks-supporter.title: Thank you message to supporter
comm-thanks-supporter.description: Warm thanks to a colleague or friend who has supported you in a difficult situation.
comm-thanks-supporter.subject: Thank you for your support / [Your Name]
comm-thanks-supporter.content:
Hi [Name],

I just wanted to thank you for being there for me [situation, e.g. in yesterday's meeting]. It really meant a lot to me.

I know my situation has been difficult, and I truly appreciate that you dared to [action, e.g. say out loud that the treatment was wrong].

Thank you for not leaving me alone.

Sincerely,
[Name]

hero.description: Psychological bullying is subtler and often more destructive than physical violence. This tool helps you name your experience.

stable.label: Stable Situation
stable.description: Your experiences currently suggest a stable work situation. Continue to nurture a good culture.

mild.label: Mild Attention
mild.description: Some signs of uncertainty are in the air. Monitor the situation and trust your instinct – often recognition is hardest at the beginning.

warning.label: Warning
warning.description: Alert signs are clear. The situation can escalate if not addressed in time. Start low-threshold documentation.

moderate.label: Increased Risk
moderate.description: Signs suggest repeated inappropriate treatment. Don't stay alone with these thoughts, but seek validation from a trusted colleague or friend.

severe.label: Severe Risk
severe.description: This is a serious situation. What you experienced corresponds to systematic bullying. We recommend contacting a union or occupational safety.

critical.label: Critical Emergency
critical.description: This is an emergency for your work ability and health. The situation suggests severe psychological violence. Seek professional help immediately.

critical_signals.title: Critical Observations
critical_signals.itsetunto: Your self-esteem is being tested. This is a typical sign of long-term invalidation.
critical_signals.todellisuus: Gaslighting signs are strong. Don't trust just your memory, document everything.
critical_signals.eristyksissä: Social isolation is detected. This is a common tactic to weaken the person's position.
critical_signals.fyysiset: Physical symptoms are strong. Your body is reacting to chronic stress. Take this seriously.
critical_signals.käyttäytyminen: Changes in behavior suggest high vigilance. You are on high alert.

tactics_page.description: Bullies often have repeating strategies. When you identify a tactic, it loses some of its power over you.

carousel.alt: Social Isolation - cut off from community
carousel.caption: One of the most common forms of bullying is social isolation – the victim is cut off from the community.
Manipulation and gaslighting are subtle but highly damaging tactics.
Verbal bullying and mockery can be as damaging as physical violence.
Ostracism is complete ignoring – as if the person does not exist.
Where are you around the table? Is someone creating a false image of you?

carousel.alt: Magnifying errors - small things blown up
carousel.caption: Even the smallest errors can be put under a magnifying glass and blown up until they overshadow everything else.
Setting goals that are impossible to achieve, or demanding performance without sufficient resources.

page.label: Situation Mapping
page.title: Is it Bullying?
page.subtitle: Go through the checklist.
page.description: This is not a diagnosis. It is a tool to help you see if the structural signs of bullying are met in your situation.
page.answer_all_hint: Answer all items to see the result.

compare_page.description: Not all corrective feedback is bullying, but bullying should not be hidden under criticism. This table helps you draw the line.
compare_page.rule_text: Constructive criticism focuses on work performance and aims for a solution. Bullying focuses on the employee and aims to harm them as a person.

comparison_points.title: Goal
comparison_points.bullying: To humiliate, control, or force out the employee.
comparison_points.criticism: To improve work quality or correct a wrong procedure.

comparison_points.title: Target
comparison_points.criticism: Performance, work results, or followed instructions.

comparison_points.title: Interaction
comparison_points.bullying: One-sided, aggressive, often in front of others or behind back.

comparison_points.title: Frequency
comparison_points.criticism: Situational and ends when the agreed change is made.

comparison_points.title: Outcome
comparison_points.bullying: Burnout, loss of self-confidence, and anxiety.
comparison_points.criticism: Clarity of expectations and professional development.

itsetunto.label: Self-Esteem
itsetunto.description: Bullying often first erodes the victim's professional and personal self-confidence.

todellisuus.label: Sense of Reality
todellisuus.description: Gaslighting and lying make the victim doubt their own perceptions and memory.

eristyksissä.label: Isolation
eristyksissä.description: Exclusion from the social circle is a powerful tool of power.

fyysiset.label: Physical Symptoms
fyysiset.description: Pressure often transfers to the body as insomnia, aches, or burnout.

käyttäytyminen.label: Behavior
käyttäytyminen.description: Permanent changes in own behavior are a sign of prolonged stress.

mitatointi.name: Invalidation & Belittling
mitatointi.definition: Constant belittling and questioning of your skills, suggestions, and achievements. The goal is to make you feel incompetent in the eyes of others and in your own mind.
phrases: That's a useless suggestion
Do you really not know this?
Anyone could have done that
Why are you making a big deal out of this?
mitatointi.goal: Erode your self-confidence, destroy your professional credibility, and limit your influence within the work community.
strategy: Document positive feedback from other colleagues and clients.
Do not expect recognition from the bully; it is a conscious decision not to give it.
Validate your skills with outside experts and networks.
mitatointi.logExample: Supervisor dismissed my suggestion as 'useless' in front of the entire team.

gaslighting.name: Gaslighting
gaslighting.definition: Psychological manipulation where the bully intentionally distorts information to make you doubt your own perceptions, memory, and mental health.
phrases: I never said that
You are too sensitive
It was a joke, don't take it hard
You are just imagining things
gaslighting.goal: Make the victim doubt their own observations, making them more easily controlled and uncertain of their own boundaries.
strategy: Write things down immediately after the event while they are fresh in your memory.
Use email and written messages to confirm all agreements.
Do not argue about memories with the bully; trust your own notes.
gaslighting.logExample: A project schedule agreed upon on Monday was completely denied on Wednesday.

uhkailu.name: Threats & Intimidation
uhkailu.definition: Direct or indirect use of fear as a tool for control and power. Threats can target employment, reputation, or social status.
phrases: I have spoken about you to management
If this repeats, you know the consequences
Maybe this field doesn't suit you
Hopefully you won't make mistakes again...
uhkailu.goal: Silence the victim, prevent defense, and force submission through fear.
strategy: Record all threats, including indirect ones and those 'between the lines'.
Contact your shop steward or occupational safety representative immediately.
Avoid being alone with the threatener; request a witness for meetings.
uhkailu.logExample: Supervisor hinted behind closed doors that my 'career continuation is at risk' if I don't agree to overtime demands.

identiteetti.name: Identity Attack
identiteetti.definition: Attack against personal traits such as age, gender, disability, origin, or other parts of identity. This is often also illegal discrimination.
phrases: Are you ADHD or why don't you focus?
Women don't understand this technical side
It's hard for someone that age to learn new things
You are so sensitive today (referring to trait)
identiteetti.goal: Humiliate the victim, demonstrate their 'inferiority', and signal that they do not belong because of a personal characteristic.
strategy: Recognize that this is often illegal discrimination (Equality and Non-Discrimination Acts).
Document words verbatim and mention any witnesses.
Contact a shop steward or the Non-Discrimination Ombudsman immediately.
identiteetti.logExample: During a training session, my age was referred to disparagingly: 'we can't expect seniors to keep up'.

sexual_harassment.name: Sexual Harassment
sexual_harassment.definition: Unwanted and offensive sexual behavior that the target does not want. It can be verbal, non-verbal, or physical.
phrases: You look good today (disparagingly)
Don't be so stiff (sexual proposition)
Double entendres and innuendos
Intrusive comments about appearance
sexual_harassment.goal: Objectify the target, exercise power, and create a humiliating or hostile environment.
strategy: State clearly and loudly: 'Stop, this is disturbing and inappropriate'.
Report the incident immediately to HR or a supervisor (if they are not the harasser).
Save all evidence: messages, photos, and notes on situations.
sexual_harassment.logExample: A colleague made several sexual comments and innuendos during lunch break.

eristaminen.name: Isolation & Exclusion
eristaminen.definition: Intentional and systematic exclusion from interaction and information flow. The goal is to make the victim invisible to others.
phrases: I forgot to tell you that
This doesn't concern you
The meeting was yesterday
(Silence when you enter the room)
eristaminen.goal: Cut off the victim's social support networks and prevent them from performing their tasks due to lack of information.
strategy: Actively build other networks inside and outside the organization.
Ask in writing for reasons for the lack of information flow and document responses.
Request meeting minutes and materials directly from the organizer.
eristaminen.logExample: The entire team went to lunch and held a planning meeting at the same time without telling me.

ostrakismi.name: Ostracism (Exclusion)
ostrakismi.definition: Complete ignoring or 'cold shoulder'. It is invisible violence where the victim is treated as if they don't exist.
phrases: (Greeting is not answered)
(Speech is interrupted when you enter)
(Conversation goes past you like you're thin air)
(Messages are completely ignored)
ostrakismi.goal: Erode the victim's psychological endurance, sense of belonging, and professional presence with silence.
strategy: Identify the situation visibly: say out loud that you greeted or asked something.
Make precise notes of observations: who failed to respond and in what situation.
Seek support and validation from occupational health or a shop steward.
ostrakismi.logExample: I have greeted colleagues for three mornings in a row, but no one has responded or looked my way.

mobbing.name: Mobbing (Group Bullying)
mobbing.definition: A situation where several members of the work community or the whole group direct inappropriate behavior at one person. Peer pressure often reinforces bullying.
phrases: Everyone thinks you're difficult
No one wants you in this project
(Shared laughter as you leave)
We have our own rules here
mobbing.goal: Sidelining the victim completely, destroying their reputation, and forcing them to resign.
strategy: Find allies outside the group or at different levels of the organization.
Report the situation immediately to senior management and HR; group bullying is an organizational risk.
Document the roles and actions of all participants as accurately as possible.
mobbing.logExample: The team signed a joint complaint about my working methods without ever discussing it with me.

maine.name: Defamation of Reputation
maine.definition: Spreading false rumors, distorting competence to others, or badmouthing the victim behind their back.
phrases: He/She is a difficult person
No one wants to work with him/her
I heard he/she makes a lot of mistakes
He/She is not a team player
maine.goal: Destroy the victim's credibility, trust, and opportunities to advance or get support in the organization.
strategy: Talk directly to colleagues and correct false information professionally during work.
Ask HR to investigate the source of rumors and demand correction of false claims.
Maintain absolute professionalism in all communication to make the defamation appear baseless.
maine.logExample: I heard that the supervisor has called me 'unstable' in front of other team members.

cyberbullying.name: Cyberbullying (Chat/Email)
cyberbullying.definition: Harassment and inappropriate behavior in digital channels (Slack, Teams, email). it often intrudes into free time.
phrases: (Disparaging memes or pictures)
(Constant questioning in chats)
(Exclusion from unofficial channels)
(Accusatory messages during free time)
cyberbullying.goal: Make free time unsafe, humiliate publicly with digital tracks, and cause constant stress.
strategy: Take screenshots of all disturbing messages immediately.
Do not respond to provocation, but take evidence forward through official channels.
Set strict technical boundaries: do not read work messages during free time.
cyberbullying.logExample: A modified image of me was shared on a Slack channel, which others laughed at with emoji reactions.

kohtuuttomuus.name: Unreasonable Demands
kohtuuttomuus.definition: Setting impossible deadlines, constantly changing instructions, or increasing the workload to a level that is impossible to handle without risking health.
phrases: This must be ready by tomorrow (4:00 PM)
Why isn't this done yet?
You need to stretch more
You are doing too little compared to others
kohtuuttomuus.goal: Exhaust the victim physically and mentally, create a cycle of failure, and provide an excuse for disciplinary action.
strategy: Document your working hours and tasks very accurately.
Ask your supervisor for a written order of priority if there are too many tasks.
Contact occupational health services if symptoms of burnout begin to appear.
kohtuuttomuus.logExample: I was given a week's worth of work on Friday afternoon to be prepared for Monday.

epaoikeudenmukaisuus.name: Injustice & Inequality
epaoikeudenmukaisuus.definition: Applying different rules to the victim compared to other colleagues. This can apply to holidays, remote work, rewards, or the division of tasks.
phrases: This doesn't apply to you
Others have different grounds
We cannot be flexible in your case
This is a new company policy (only for you)
epaoikeudenmukaisuus.goal: Weaken the victim's position, cause bitterness, and signal that they are not an equal member of the work community.
strategy: Request written reasons for why the practice differs in your case.
Compare your situation with the organization's official guidelines and HR policy.
Take the matter up with HR or a shop steward as discrimination.
epaoikeudenmukaisuus.logExample: Everyone else received approval for remote work, but in my case, it was denied without grounds.

micromanagement.name: Micromanagement & Tracking
micromanagement.definition: Constant, almost obsessive control of work and interference in details. it signals a complete lack of trust in your expertise.
phrases: Put me as a copy in every email
Why did you use this font?
Tell me exactly what you do every hour
I want to see every draft immediately
micromanagement.goal: Paralyze the victim's independent decision-making, erode professional self-esteem, and create a sense of being under constant surveillance.
strategy: Agree on clear reporting intervals and 'rules of the game' in writing.
Ask directly: 'You seem concerned about the quality of my work, how can we build trust?'
Document the time spent on tracking, which is away from actual work.
micromanagement.logExample: Supervisor requires an hourly report from me on everything I do, even though others don't have to.

credit_stealing.name: Credit Stealing
credit_stealing.definition: Presenting another person's work, ideas, or results as one's own. Often a supervisor or a manipulative colleague takes the credit for a successful project.
phrases: I decided that we should do this
I managed to finish this
My idea worked really well
I did the bulk of the work here
credit_stealing.goal: Weaken the victim's career development opportunities and shift positive attention and rewards to the bully.
strategy: Leave digital tracks in the work in your own name (version control, emails).
Speak openly about your work progress and ideas to other colleagues and management too.
Take the matter up: 'It was great that my idea X worked, as I wrote in my report'.
credit_stealing.logExample: Supervisor presented an analysis made by me to the executive board as their own work without mentioning me at all.

unjustified_warnings.name: Unjustified Warnings
unjustified_warnings.definition: Giving warnings or official notes without actual negligence or poor work performance. it is often preparation for dismissal.
phrases: This is an official note
Your performance is substandard
I have received complaints about your work (unspecified)
This will be recorded in the personnel register
unjustified_warnings.goal: Create a 'blacklist' to remove the victim from the organization in a seemingly legal way.
strategy: Do not sign any warning whose content you do not agree with; write 'received but contested'.
Demand written evidence and a breakdown of the alleged errors.
Contact a union lawyer or shop steward immediately.
unjustified_warnings.logExample: I received a written warning for 'bad attitude', even though my targets have been filled 110%.

passiivi-aggressio.name: Passive-Aggression
passiivi-aggressio.definition: Expressing anger and resistance indirectly, such as through procrastination, 'forgetting', silence, or mocking comments dismissed as a joke.
phrases: Yes, I'll do it (doesn't do it)
How 'efficient' you are today (mockingly)
Oh, I forgot to tell you again
There's no problem here, believe me...
passiivi-aggressio.goal: Cause confusion and frustration in the victim without the bully having to take direct responsibility for their behavior.
strategy: Stay calm and professional; passive-aggression feeds on emotional reaction.
Ask clarifying questions: 'What did you mean by that comment?'
Confirm all oral agreements immediately by email.
passiivi-aggressio.logExample: A colleague sighs and rolls their eyes every time I speak in a meeting, but says 'everything is fine' when asked.

thousand-cuts.name: Death by a Thousand Cuts
thousand-cuts.definition: Constant repetition of small, seemingly insignificant negative things. A single act doesn't look like bullying, but their sum destroys the victim.
phrases: Just a small note
Don't be offended by something like that
This is just feedback
Again that same small thing
thousand-cuts.goal: Erode the victim's resilience and self-confidence slowly so that the situation is not easy to point out to outsiders.
strategy: Keep a precise logbook of all even small events; the big picture is most important.
Take the matter up as a 'phenomenon', not just a single act.
Talk about your observations to peers or occupational safety to prove systematicity.
thousand-cuts.logExample: Daily joking about my name, ignoring at the coffee table, and small but constant error-finding.

sarcasm_mockery.name: Sarcasm & Mockery
sarcasm_mockery.definition: Using humor as an attack. Mockery and ridicule are hidden behind joking, and protests are met by accusing the victim of lacking a sense of humor.
phrases: That was another 'brilliant' idea
Your sense of humor is a bit lost
Look at our 'expert' here
Don't be so thin-skinned, it was a joke
sarcasm_mockery.goal: Humiliate and silence the victim socially so they cannot defend themselves without being labeled a 'spoilsport'.
strategy: Do not laugh along if it feels bad; maintain a neutral expression.
State directly: 'That didn't feel like a joke, but an insult'.
Ask: 'Could you explain the point of the joke? I don't understand it'. This forces the mocker to explain their stupidity.
sarcasm_mockery.logExample: Supervisor joked about my skills at the entire department's Christmas party, making others laugh uncomfortably.

neglect_indifference.name: Indifference & Neglect
neglect_indifference.definition: Completely ignoring the victim's needs, questions, or work contribution. it signals that the victim or their work has no significance to the organization.
phrases: We'll look at that sometime (never)
I don't have time for you
That is not a priority now
(No response to feedback requests)
neglect_indifference.goal: Invalidate the victim's professional existence and make them feel completely insignificant and useless.
strategy: Demand official development discussions and feedback in writing.
Make your work visible to other stakeholders to get appreciation from elsewhere.
Document repeated failures to respond and being ignored.
neglect_indifference.logExample: I have asked the supervisor for guidance on a critical project four times over a month without any response.

withholding_info.name: Withholding Information
withholding_info.definition: Hiding or delaying information necessary for performing work. The victim gets the information too late or incomplete.
phrases: Oh, did no one tell you?
This just came in (lie)
I thought you already knew
It's between us for now
withholding_info.goal: Make the victim fail, make mistakes, and look bad in the eyes of management.
strategy: Create your own information sources and network extensively in the organization.
When you notice a lack of information, ask immediately in writing: 'Who is handling this? From whom can I get more information?'
Report deficiencies in information flow as risks to the project's success.
withholding_info.logExample: The project deadline was moved earlier, but I was only told on the deadline day.

triangulation.name: Triangulation
triangulation.definition: The bully does not speak directly to the victim but uses a third party to convey messages, spread rumors, or sow suspicion between employees.
phrases: X said that you are a bit slow
Everyone else is worried about you
Better if X doesn't know about this
In X's opinion, your project is failing
triangulation.goal: Isolate the victim, destroy trust between colleagues, and control the situation by controlling the flow of information.
strategy: Speak directly to the people the bully uses as 'intermediaries'.
Say to the third party: 'If you or X have feedback, I would appreciate it directly to me'.
Do not blindly believe what the bully claims others have said.
triangulation.logExample: Supervisor claimed colleague X had criticized my work, but when speaking with X, it turned out to be a lie.

scapegoating.name: Scapegoating
scapegoating.definition: Blaming one person for the mistakes, failures, or bad atmosphere of a group or supervisor, even if they were not responsible for the matter.
phrases: This is all your fault
If you hadn't done X, the situation would be different
You are the weakest link in the team
Because of you, we didn't get this finished
scapegoating.goal: Shift focus away from real problems or the bully's own incompetence and find a target for collective blame.
strategy: Document exactly who did what and what the areas of responsibility were in the project.
Bring up the facts: 'This decision was made together at point Y, and my own responsibilities were limited to Z'.
Request an outside audit or investigation into the reasons for the failure.
scapegoating.logExample: The entire department's budget overrun was blamed on me, even though I am not responsible for the budget.

concern_trolling.name: Concern Trolling
concern_trolling.definition: Aggression disguised as care. The bully pretends to be worried about the victim's coping or health but uses it as a way to belittle or ignore them.
phrases: Are you quite alright now?
Should you take sick leave (when you disagree)?
We are all worried about your mental health
Maybe this task is too heavy for you now...
concern_trolling.goal: Create an image of an unstable or incapable employee and bypass their professional opinions on 'health' grounds.
strategy: Respond firmly: 'Thank you for your concern, I am completely fine and able to handle my work'.
Turn the conversation back to the issues: 'Let's discuss this project now, not speculate on my well-being'.
Document care-related comments if they are repeated whenever there are setbacks or disagreements.
concern_trolling.logExample: Whenever I questioned the supervisor's decision, they started asking 'if I've slept enough' and 'if I need help coping'.

victim_playing.name: Playing the Victim
victim_playing.definition: Manipulation where the bully turns the situation so that they are the one being treated badly when the victim tries to defend themselves or set boundaries.
phrases: You are attacking me
Why do you always blame me?
I'm just trying to help, and I get this
I have such a hard time with you
victim_playing.goal: Take focus away from their own bad behavior, cause guilt in the victim, and gather pity and support from others.
strategy: Stay strictly with the facts: 'I am not attacking, but pointing out that an attachment was missing from this message'.
Do not apologize for things you have not done wrong, even if the other person's feelings are hurt by your boundaries.
Describe the situation to a third party: 'I set a boundary, and the other party reacted in this way'.
victim_playing.logExample: When I asked a colleague to stop mocking, they started crying and said I was 'bullying' them with my demands.

manipulaatio.name: Emotional Manipulation
manipulaatio.definition: Using emotions (guilt, fear, sense of duty) to guide the victim's actions. The bully often alternates between 'good' and 'bad' to keep the victim on their toes.
phrases: If you are my friend, you'll do this
Do you really think anyone else would tolerate you?
We did so much for you
You owe me this
manipulaatio.goal: Make the victim act against their own interests and bind them emotionally to the bully.
strategy: Identify the 'hot and cold' alternation; it's part of the control mechanism.
Keep relationships purely professional and avoid personal confidences with a manipulator.
Trust your gut: if you are being made to feel guilty about work tasks, it is manipulation.
manipulaatio.logExample: Supervisor praised me to the skies in the morning, but in the afternoon yelled at me in front of others for a trivial matter.

resources_denial.name: Resource Denial
resources_denial.definition: Denying tools, budget, time, or assisting personnel needed to perform work, even if they are essential for achieving goals.
phrases: You have to manage with this
We don't have a budget for your department
Everyone else manages to be on time
You don't need new tools
resources_denial.goal: Sabotage the victim's success, cause extreme stress, and create grounds for underperformance.
strategy: Make a written report on missing resources and their impact on the outcome.
Report deficiencies to occupational safety as a risk to work safety and coping.
Request official prioritization: 'What tasks should we leave undone because tool X is missing?'
resources_denial.logExample: I was denied access to software without which finishing the report is impossible, but the deadline remained the same.

underemployment.name: Underemployment
underemployment.definition: Giving tasks that are too easy, trivial, or humiliating relative to professional skill (e.g., placing an expert to just do archiving). It is also called 'invisible dismissal'.
phrases: This is your new area of responsibility now (copying)
We don't dare give you anything bigger
Be happy that you even have something to do
This is at your level now
underemployment.goal: Humiliate and frustrate a professional so much that they resign 'voluntarily' themselves.
strategy: Do the given tasks perfectly so that your competence cannot be questioned.
Ask for written reasons for the change in job description and compare them to your employment contract.
Actively seek new challenges or a transfer elsewhere in the organization.
underemployment.logExample: After years of experience, I was moved away from projects just to mail letters.

moving_goalposts.name: Moving the Goalposts
moving_goalposts.definition: Changing the criteria for success on the fly. When the victim achieves a goal, the bully claims something else is more important or reproaches the outcome on new grounds.
phrases: I didn't mean that
That is not enough now
This is not what I asked for (even though they did)
Now we have to do this completely differently
moving_goalposts.goal: Keep the victim in constant uncertainty, prevent a sense of success, and create grounds for 'poor performance'.
strategy: Request goals and acceptance criteria always in writing and have them approved before starting work.
When the line changes, show the original agreement and ask for the reasons for the change.
Save all change requests in chronological order as evidence of the confusion of instructions.
moving_goalposts.logExample: I finished the project according to instructions, but the supervisor said 'I should have realized to do it completely differently' without previous guidance.

spatial_harassment.name: Spatial Harassment
spatial_harassment.definition: Deteriorating or harassing the victim's physical work environment. Moving to a noisy place, a warehouse, away from others, or constant rummaging through the victim's workstation.
phrases: This is your place now (even though there are empty ones elsewhere)
Others need more peace
We were just looking for something on your desk
You must be here so I can supervise you
spatial_harassment.goal: Cause physical discomfort, signal worthlessness, and violate the victim's privacy and peace.
strategy: Request official occupational safety grounds for the location of the workstation.
Say clearly: 'I would prefer that people do not visit my workstation without permission; it disturbs my concentration'.
Document physical conditions (noise, lighting, ergonomics) and their deficiencies.
spatial_harassment.logExample: My workstation was moved next to the photocopier in the hallway away from the rest of the team, where constant noise prevented work.

symbolic_demotion.name: Symbolic Demotion
symbolic_demotion.definition: Undermining status with gestures and actions: removing the title from communication, leaving the name off lists, or treating the victim as if they were an intern, even if they are an experienced expert.
phrases: You are just an assistant here
We don't need titles here (only in your case)
Your name was forgotten from the door again
Better ask X, they know better (even though you know yourself)
symbolic_demotion.goal: Signal to others and to the victim themselves that they no longer have power, status, or appreciation in the work community.
strategy: Use your title and signature consistently yourself in all communication.
Point out missing information professionally: 'I noticed my name was missing from the list of participants, could you fix this?'.
Make your expertise visible through the results of high-quality work.
symbolic_demotion.logExample: My name was removed from the project steering group list, but the work and responsibilities still remained with me.

scenarios.text: A supervisor gives strict feedback on a late report and demands immediate corrections.
scenarios.explanation: Professional feedback on work and management requires direction, which is not bullying even if it feels unpleasant.

scenarios.text: A colleague repeatedly leaves one team member out of lunch invites, even though everyone else is asked.
scenarios.explanation: Isolation and exclusion are some of the most typical forms of social bullying.

scenarios.text: A supervisor points out a mistake in front of the whole team and sarcastically mocks the employee's skills.
scenarios.explanation: Public humiliation and questioning competence in an inappropriate way is bullying.

scenarios.text: An employee is given new, challenging tasks that they are qualified for but that require learning.
scenarios.explanation: Changing job descriptions or challenging employees is not bullying if based on work needs and not unreasonable.

scenarios.text: User accounts are 'accidentally' closed multiple times a month right before important deadlines.
scenarios.explanation: Sabotaging work is systematic bullying aimed at destabilizing the victim's position.

scenarios.text: An employee receives an invitation to change negotiations along with the rest of the department.
scenarios.explanation: Statutory employer actions, such as change negotiations, are not bullying.

scenarios.text: An employee's free-time hobbies are repeatedly laughed at in the break room.
scenarios.explanation: Mockery and insults directed at personal life constitute bullying.

scenarios.text: A team member disagrees with your idea in a weekly meeting and presents opposing arguments.
scenarios.explanation: Disagreements and debating issues are part of a normal work community.

scenarios.text: All responsibilities are taken away from an employee without justification, leaving them with no tasks.
scenarios.explanation: Leaving someone with empty tasks is passive bullying aimed at crushing the employee.

scenarios.text: False rumors about an employee's private life are spread at the workplace.
scenarios.explanation: Harassment directed at reputation and gossiping is clear bullying.

scenarios.text: The supervisor asks for an explanation for repeated Monday absences.
scenarios.explanation: The employer has the right and duty to monitor absences and address them.

scenarios.text: An employee is constantly given impossible deadlines known to be unachievable.
scenarios.explanation: Exhausting someone with unreasonable demands is a form of workplace bullying.

scenarios.text: The work community has a loud volume and stressful atmosphere due to rush.
scenarios.explanation: A bad atmosphere or rush is not automatically bullying if it doesn't target any specific individual.

scenarios.text: An employee is consistently interrupted in meetings or not listened to.
scenarios.explanation: Restricting speech and ignoring is silencing, which is bullying.

scenarios.text: Workplace rules (e.g., working hours) are applied strictly to all employees.
scenarios.explanation: Equitable application of rules is not bullying.

scenarios.text: An employee's emails are not answered for weeks, even though matters require decisions from others.
scenarios.explanation: Withholding information and not responding to hinder work is bullying.

scenarios.text: The person perceived as a bully is stressed and exhausted themselves.
scenarios.explanation: Bullying doesn't stop, even if the perpetrator's motive is burnout. The action remains bullying.

scenarios.text: At the workplace Christmas party, someone jokes tastelessly on a general level.
scenarios.explanation: Bad behavior or tasteless humor is unpleasant, but not yet bullying if it is a one-off and not directed at anyone.

scenarios.text: An employee is granted a smaller bonus than others due to weaker results.
scenarios.explanation: Justified different treatment (e.g., performance pay) is not bullying.

scenarios.text: The supervisor moves an employee's workstation to a cleaning closet without a work-related reason.
scenarios.explanation: Physical isolation and humiliating space arrangements are clear bullying.

results.title: Your
results.immediate_support: You need immediate support for your situation.
results.severe_load: You are experiencing severe and systematic strain.
results.active_action: Your situation requires active monitoring and action.
results.manageable: Your situation seems manageable at the moment.
results.remember_text: These results do not define your worth as a person. They only measure how heavily your current environment affects you. You do not deserve this. Turvasiipi is here to help you build a path back to safety.

questions.question: I often think: "I am too sensitive" or "I take things too heavily"
questions.validationText: 68% of workplace bullying victims think this. This thought is often a result of gaslighting, where your feelings have been repeatedly trivialized. You are NOT too sensitive.

questions.question: I doubt my professional skills or competence (even though my results are objectively good)
questions.validationText: 71% of victims start doubting their competence. If you have been constantly criticized or invalidated, it erodes your self-confidence despite real results.

questions.question: I compare myself to others and think: "Others are coping, why not me?"
questions.validationText: 62% of victims compare themselves to others. Remember that you are treated differently than others. It's not about coping, but an uneven playing field.

questions.question: I think that I deserve this treatment or that "maybe there is something wrong with me"
questions.validationText: 54% of victims start believing they deserve the treatment. No one deserves humiliation or fear. The fault lies with the bully and structures, not you.

questions.question: I apologize for things that are not my fault
questions.validationText: Constant apologizing is a survival mechanism in a toxic environment. You don't need to apologize for your existence or things you cannot influence.

questions.question: I think that "if only I were better/tried harder, this would stop"
questions.validationText: This is a common fallacy. Bullying is not about your performance, but power. You cannot 'earn' good treatment by being better – it is your fundamental right.

questions.question: I feel alone with this
questions.validationText: 72% of victims feel alone. Isolation is a deliberate bullying tactic to deprive the victim of support and external validation.

questions.question: I fear that no one will believe me if I tell
questions.validationText: 68% of victims fear disbelief. Bullying is often subtle and happens behind closed doors, which feeds this fear.

questions.question: Others do not intervene, so I think that "maybe this is normal"
questions.validationText: 58% of victims interpret others' silence as approval. In reality, others often fear becoming targets themselves and freeze.

questions.question: I cannot talk about this to anyone
questions.validationText: 63% of victims feel they cannot talk to anyone. Shame is the bully's strongest weapon. Speaking up is the first step to breaking the power.

questions.question: I think that HR/management will not help because they protect the company/bully
questions.validationText: 55% of victims share this concern. It is important to document everything carefully and seek help outside the organization if necessary.

questions.question: I don't know what to do next
questions.validationText: This is a normal trauma response. Excessive stress paralyzes decision-making. Turvasiipi helps you take one small step at a time.

questions.question: I fear the situation will get worse if I try to intervene
questions.validationText: 69% of victims fear retaliation. That is why it is important to build evidence (documentation) before you officially raise the issue.

questions.question: I don't have the strength to fight or try anymore
questions.validationText: 76% of victims feel exhaustion. Your body is telling you that you have fought too long and too alone. Now is the time to rest and seek support.

questions.question: I think that "I should just endure this" or "I am not a victim"
questions.validationText: 61% of victims try to 'just endure'. Enduring does not stop bullying, it only consumes your health. Seeking help is courage, not weakness.

questions.question: My memory has weakened - I don't remember exactly what happened
questions.validationText: 48% of victims suffer from memory problems. Constant stress affects the brain's memory center. That is why documenting immediately after events is critical.

questions.question: I fear going to work (especially on Monday mornings)
questions.validationText: Monday anxiety is a serious sign of insecurity. Your body warns you of an unhealthy environment before you are even there.

questions.question: I don't know when the 'next blow' will come - I am in a constant state of alertness
questions.validationText: 67% of victims live in a 'fight or flight' state. This consumes the nervous system and is a typical PTSD symptom. You need a safe distance to recover.

questions.question: I fear losing my job if I speak up / report
questions.validationText: 71% of victims fear for their job. However, the law protects the reporter from retaliation. Documentation is your best protection against illegal actions.

questions.question: Work matters follow me home - messages or thoughts take over free time
questions.validationText: When work follows you home as nightmares or thoughts, recovery is prevented. This is one of the strongest predictors of burnout and trauma.

questions.question: I am no longer myself - my personality has changed
questions.validationText: 64% of victims feel they have lost themselves. This is not permanent, but it tells how deep long-term bullying strikes.

questions.question: I have lost my joy - things that used to delight me no longer interest me
questions.validationText: 68% of victims suffer from loss of joy. It is a symptom of depression and burnout that requires stopping and often professional help.

questions.question: I remember how I was before - and I would like to be that person again
questions.validationText: 59% of victims miss their 'former self'. That person has not disappeared, they are just traumatized and protecting themselves. Recovery is the path back.

questions.question: I look in the mirror and don't recognize myself
questions.validationText: 41% of victims feel estranged from themselves. Body and mind can create distance from painful reality. This is a sign to seek help.

questions.question: I don't sleep properly - I wake up at night or suffer from nightmares
questions.validationText: Insomnia is the body's way of screaming about overload. Sleep is critical for recovery, and its constant disruption requires reaction.

questions.question: I have stomach issues or nausea especially before work
questions.validationText: 58% of victims suffer from stomach symptoms. Your body reacts to fear physically before your mind has time to analyze the situation.

questions.question: My heart pounds or I feel anxiety in work situations
questions.validationText: 64% of victims experience anxiety symptoms. It is the body's natural alarm system against an unjust and threatening situation.

questions.question: I have been sick more often this year than before
questions.validationText: 58% of victims get sick more often. Long-term stress and high cortisol weaken your immune system.

questions.question: I use alcohol, medication, or other means to cope
questions.validationText: 31% of victims resort to substances to numb their pain. It is a human reaction to unbearable feeling, but exhausts the body further.

questions.question: I have considered suicide or feel that life has no meaning
questions.validationText: This is the most serious possible sign. You are not alone, and help is available 24/7. Call the crisis helpline immediately: 09 2525 0111.
